studies.question: When going for it on 4th down gains win probability, how often do NFL teams go?
studies.answer: In states where going gains 1+ WP point, teams went 25% of the time in 2015-16 and 45% in 2024-25.
findings: Clear-kick states: teams go about 4% of the time every season (n=15,129).
WP lost to clear errors: 4.6 WP pts per team-game in 2015-16 (4.3-4.9), 3.4 in 2024-25 (3.2-3.7).
studies.method: Per play, expected WPA of go (pooled conversion rate x WPA if converted/failed) vs best of punt/FG, each from boosted models of nflverse WPA on the same pre-snap state, cross-fit by game. Teams' own choice does not set the rate. WP-lost CIs exclude model error.
studies.data: nflverse play-by-play, 2015 to 2026 wk 8, Q1-Q4 4th downs (no penalties/kneels), 44,765 plays, 3,148 games.
studies.split_check: Model checks out of sample: realized WPA in go states, goers +1.3 vs kickers -1.3 pts (n=4,866/8,682); rise in go rate holds every season.

studies.question: Down 14 in the 4th, should a team go for two after the first touchdown?
studies.answer: Yes. With two TDs and a stop, going for 2 first wins 59% vs 47% kicking. Teams went for 2 54% of the time in 2025-26.
findings: Win chance gain given two TDs: +12.1 pts (+9.7 to +14.4).
Down 8 at a Q4 PAT: went for 2 in 2 of 72 in 2015-18, 13 of 24 in 2025-26.
The early 2-pt result also tells the team whether it needs a TD or a TD and 2 on the next drive.
studies.method: Closed-form win chance given two TDs and no opponent score, with pooled 2-pt and XP rates; CI from Beta draws of both rates. Go-for-2 share counts Q4 tries at down 8, Wilson CIs.
studies.data: nflverse play-by-play, 2015 to 2026 wk 8; 193 Q4 PATs at down 8; 1,458 2-pt tries.
studies.split_check: Gain holds with 2015-20 rates (+11.7 pts) and 2021-26 rates (+12.3 pts).

studies.question: Do surprise onside kicks get recovered more than expected late-game onside kicks?
studies.answer: Yes, 25% vs 9% (2015-23), but below the ~32% break-even for an early onside. Net WPA not different from zero.
findings: Q1-Q3 surprise onside, kicking-team WPA -0.6 pts (-1.8 to +0.6, n=54); normal kickoff -0.04.
Break-even recovery rate for a Q1-Q3 surprise onside: about 32%.
2024-26 expected onsides: 6.3% recovered (3.2-11.9, n=127).
studies.method: Onside = kickoff described as onside. Expected = Q4 with the kicker trailing; surprise = all others. WPA compared with normal Q1-Q3 kickoffs within 14 points, game bootstrap CIs. Teams pick spots, so rates are upper bounds.
studies.data: nflverse play-by-play, 2015 to 2026 wk 8, 691 onside kicks.
studies.split_check: Surprise recovery 28% in 2015-18 (n=32), 21% in 2019-23 (n=24); expected stays near 9%.

studies.question: On 3rd or 4th and 1, does the QB sneak convert more often than other plays?
studies.answer: Yes. Sneaks convert 82%, other runs 69%, passes 56%. Sneak share of these plays was 8% in 2015, 14% in 2025.
findings: Pass 56.3% (54.4-58.2, n=2,612). Gap sneak minus other run +12.5 pts (+10.1 to +14.9).
EPA per play: sneak +0.33 (+0.23 to +0.42), other run +0.04, pass -0.14.
Without PHI and BUF, sneaks still convert 81.1% (78.7-83.3, n=1,102).

rq.q: On 3rd or 4th and 1, does the QB sneak convert more often than other plays?
rq.a: Yes. Sneaks convert 82%, other runs 69%, passes 56%. Sneak share of these plays was 8% in 2015, 14% in 2025.

studies.question: Is a two-point try worth more than an extra point on average?
studies.answer: No clear edge. 2-pt tries score 0.96 points per try, XPs 0.94; difference +0.02 (-0.03 to +0.07).
findings: 2-pt success 48.1% (45.5-50.6, n=1,458); break-even vs XP is 47.2%.
2-pt rate by season ranges 41% to 55%; every season CI includes 48%.

studies.answer: No clear edge: leader wins 92.7% fouling, 91.4% defending; +2.3 pp at equal time (CI -2.4 to +6.4).

studies.method: First trailer possession per game that is live with 12 s or less, final regulation period, down 3. Foul = leader's non-shooting foul sending trailer to the line before any shot. Compared within possession-start bins (4-8, 8-12, 12+ s); outcome = game win incl. OT.

studies.question: Does a timeout stop an opponent run?
studies.answer: No: after an 8+ pt run, a timeout nets -0.31 pts over the next 2:00 vs playing on (CI -0.40 to -0.23).
findings: Timeout: next 2:00 net +0.51 pts (CI +0.44 to +0.58), n=9313.
No timeout: next 2:00 net +0.83 pts (CI +0.79 to +0.87), n=23790.
Both groups outscore the opponent after the run (mean reversion plus the ball); same-state gap -0.31.
Q4 only: timeout minus none -0.26 pts (CI -0.42 to -0.10), n=6980.
studies.method: Trigger = score making an unanswered run 8+ pts, >= 2:30 left in quarter, margin within 20. Timeout in that dead ball vs no timeout in next 60 s; net points next 120 s; matched on run size and quarter.

studies.question: Up 3 in the last 12 seconds, should the leader foul or defend?
studies.answer: Foul: leader wins 93.6% fouling, 92.4% defending; +2.8 pp at equal time (CI +0.8 to +4.6).
findings: Same-time difference (foul minus defend): +2.8 pp (95% CI +0.8 to +4.6).
Reached OT: foul 6.7%, defend 14.2%. Lost in regulation: foul 3.1%, defend 0.9%.
Leader win rate once in OT: foul 50.7% (n=71), defend 52.7% (n=857).
studies.method: First trailer possession per game that is live with 12 s or less, final regulation period, down 3. Foul = leader's non-shooting foul sending trailer to the line before any shot. Compared within possession-start bins (4-8, 8-12, 12+ s); outcome = game win incl. OT.
studies.data: ESPN play-by-play via sportsdataverse, CBB, 2011-12 to 2025-26, 7,116 games.

studies.question: Does a timeout before a late free throw make the shooter miss?
studies.answer: Icing does not work: iced shooters +2.3 pp vs un-iced, relative to own FT% (CI +0.0 to +4.6).
findings: Iced: 71.2% made (CI 68.9-73.4), shooters' usual 72.5%, n=1567.
Not iced: 69.9% made (CI 69.5-70.2), shooters' usual 73.4%, n=59853.
Iced minus not iced, vs own FT%: +2.3 pp (95% CI +0.0 to +4.6).
studies.method: First FT of a trip, last 2:00 of regulation or OT, margin within 3. Iced = defense timeout between foul and FT. Outcome = made minus shooter's leave-one-out FT% (min 20 other FTs); game-clustered bootstrap.
studies.data: ESPN play-by-play via sportsdataverse, CBB, 2011-12 to 2025-26, 61,420 first free throws.
studies.split_check: Iced minus not iced: +2.0 pp in 2012-19 (CI -1.0 to +4.8), +2.5 in 2020-26 (CI -0.8 to +6.1).

studies.question: When should a trailing team pull its goalie?
studies.answer: Pull at 3:18 down one, 6:27 down two. Teams pull at 1:52 and 2:39.
findings: Optimum CI: 2:42-3:57 down 1, 4:42-9:04 down 2. 2% of down-1 pulls (n=1,801) come that early.
Gain vs actual timing from 10:00 left, down 1: +0.6 pts tie chance (0.2 to 1.2).
studies.method: Outcome: level or ahead at 60:00. Per-second Markov model on goal rates by state (6v5, 5v5 down 1/2, tied), game-cluster bootstrap CIs. Model matches observed: down 1 at 6:00, 22.5% predicted vs 24.4% observed (n=1,523).
studies.data: NHL API play-by-play + shift charts, regular seasons 2021-22 to 2024-25, 5,248 games; pull times from goalie shifts.

rq.q: When should a trailing team pull its goalie?
rq.a: Pull at 3:18 down one, 6:27 down two. Teams pull at 1:52 and 2:39.
rq.note: n = 5,248 · level at 60:00 % by minutes left when pulled (down 1)

studies.question: Should a team down one late pull its goalie on a power play?
studies.answer: Yes with 3:00 or less left: 6v4 adds 8 pts of tie chance at 2:00. Past 4:00 the gain is not clear.
findings: 5v4 trailing, 3rd period: 8.5 GF/60 (7.9-9.1), 1.2 GA/60; 5,159 min.
Minor at 2:00 left, down 1: 31% level at 60:00 with 6v4 vs 24% at 5v4 (diff CI 3 to 12 pts).
Minor at 4:00 left: +3.7 pts (-0.4 to 7.6), not distinguishable from zero.
studies.method: Outcome: level or ahead at 60:00. Markov model, 2:00 minor: 6v4 vs 5v4 then optimal even-strength pull; rates from trailing teams in the 3rd period. 6v4 time is chosen late, so its rates carry selection.
studies.data: NHL API play-by-play + shift charts, regular seasons 2021-22 to 2024-25, 5,248 games.
studies.split_check: Gain at 2:00 left: +9 pts in 2021-23, +6 pts in 2023-25.

studies.question: After the 2023 base and pickoff rules, do runners still steal too little?
studies.answer: Slightly. Steals of 2nd succeed 75.9% vs 71.7% break-even, +2.6 runs per team-season. At 1 out, no edge.
findings: Attempts per PA with runner on 1st only: 6.0% to 8.3%. Success fell each year: 77.2%, 75.8%, 74.8%.
studies.method: Steal attempts from clean states (runner on 1st only, or 2nd only), incl. pickoff-CS and K+CS. Break-even from era RE24 (innings 1-8). Run value uses the steal outcome only. Average success above break-even does not prove the marginal try pays.
studies.data: Retrosheet play-by-play, 2021-2025 regular season, 15,011 steal attempts in clean states. Retrosheet: the information used here was obtained free of charge from and is copyrighted by Retrosheet (www.retrosheet.org).
studies.split_check: Success above break-even in each season 2023, 2024, 2025 for steals of 2nd; gap shrinks from +4.1% to +3.3%.

studies.question: Do intentional walks gain win probability for the defense?
studies.answer: Mostly no. Runner on 2nd, 1 out: IBB costs the defense 2.0 win-prob pts. Other states: no gain distinguishable from 0.
findings: Runner on 2nd, 1 out: -2.0 pts (CI -3.3 to -0.7), n=545 IBB; late and close -4.1 pts (CI -7.1 to -1.2).
2nd and 3rd, 1 out: +1.3 pts (CI +0.9 to +1.8) over the PA but +0.3 (CI -0.8 to +1.4) to end of inning.
IBB batters: +15 pts of season wOBA over other batters in these states; in the model.
IBB per season: 826 in 2016, 393 in 2025 (non-pitcher batters, innings 1-9).
studies.method: Defense-view change in empirical WE, from the PA start to the end of the half-inning (main) and over the PA. OLS with batter and on-deck season wOBA, inning x score x season cells; SE clustered by game. Compared with pitching to the batter in the same state.
studies.data: Retrosheet play-by-play, 2015-2025 regular season, 6,129 intentional walks to non-pitchers in innings 1-9. Retrosheet: the information used here was obtained free of charge from and is copyrighted by Retrosheet (www.retrosheet.org).

studies.question: Does the times-through-the-order penalty justify pulling starters before the 3rd time?
studies.answer: For an average starter, yes. 3rd time: +.022 wOBA vs 1st (same pitcher), .339 vs relievers .323.
findings: Within pitcher-season: 2nd time +.013 (CI +.011 to +.016), 3rd time +.022 (CI +.020 to +.025) wOBA vs 1st.
Pitch count adds nothing: -.004 (CI -.012 to +.004) per 100 pitches; 3rd time stays +.025.
Jump at batter 19: +.017 (SE .003) in 2015-19, +.000 (SE .003) in 2020-25, a smooth rise instead.
Batter-adjusted wOBA: starters 1st time .321, 3rd time .339; relievers inn. 6+ .323 (n=664,061).
studies.method: OLS on PA wOBA with pitcher-season fixed effects, batter-season wOBA, platoon and home; SE clustered by game. Survivors to the 3rd time are pitchers having better days, so the penalty is if anything understated.
studies.data: Retrosheet play-by-play, 2015-2025 regular season, 1,109,963 starter PAs (1st-3rd time), 24,958 games. Retrosheet: the information used here was obtained free of charge from and is copyrighted by Retrosheet (www.retrosheet.org).
studies.split_check: 3rd-time penalty +.024 in 2015-19 and +.020 in 2020-25; discrete jumps only in 2015-19.

studies.question: Does a team leading by one goal lose the xG battle late, and does it cost points?
studies.answer: Yes after 75': xG share 46% vs 53% expected. Costs 0.05 xPts from 75', but actual points held.
findings: Leading by 1, 75-90+: xG share 45.9% (CI 43.2%-48.4%), expected 52.7%, 1434 matches.
Leader xG/90 75-90+: 1.16 for, 1.38 against. 15-45': share 57% and 55%, expected 54%.
Up 1 at 75' (n=1041): xPts 2.55 from realized xG vs 2.60 at strength rates; gap -0.05 (CI -0.08 to -0.03).
Actual points 2.60 (CI 2.55-2.65), vs 2.60 baseline (gap 0.00). Late xG lost does not show up in results.
studies.method: 11v11 minutes only, split by score state and 15-min band. Expected share from leave-one-out season xG for/against of both teams, home factor, and league xG volume by band. xPts from Poisson on remaining xG; CIs bootstrap by match.

studies.question: Do teams score more or less in the minutes after a goal?
studies.answer: No momentum swing. Team that just conceded scores 0.95x baseline in the next 10 min; scorer 1.06x. Restart dips the first 3 min.
findings: Team that conceded, 0-10 min: xG 0.92x baseline (CI 0.88-0.96), goals 0.95x (CI 0.88-1.02).
Team that scored, 0-10 min: xG 0.99x (CI 0.95-1.03), goals 1.06x (CI 0.99-1.12).
First 3 min after a goal both teams sit below baseline (xG 0.74x and 0.87x): restart time.
No sign a team is most vulnerable just after scoring: its opponent's goals 0-10 min are 0.95x baseline.
studies.method: Team-minutes (11v11) by time since last goal. Baseline: league rate for the same 15-min band and score state, scaled by pre-match strength (leave-one-out season xG). Observed/expected; CIs bootstrap by match.

rq.q: Do teams score more or less in the minutes after a goal?
rq.a: No momentum swing. Team that just conceded scores 0.95x baseline in the next 10 min; scorer 1.06x. Restart dips the first 3 min.
rq.note: n = 2,856 · observed / expected xG by minutes since goal (team that conceded)

studies.question: When do teams make their first sub by score state, and does an early first sub pay off?
studies.answer: Trailing teams sub first by 60', level and leading by 65'. A first sub before 60' adds +0.04 xG diff; no goal effect found.
findings: First tactical sub at HT: trailing 34.4% (n=1606), level 16.0% (n=2206), leading 13.0% (n=1582).
Subbed by 60' if state held: trailing 60%, level 36%, leading 30%.
Sub before 60' vs none, 60' to end: xG diff +0.041 (CI +0.005 to +0.078), goal diff +0.045 (CI -0.02 to +0.11); n=4,853.
Trailing at 60': +0.070 xG diff (CI +0.004 to +0.136, n=1699). HT subs vs none: +0.052 (CI -0.002 to +0.105).
studies.method: Timing: discrete hazard of first tactical sub per minute by current state. Effect: landmark at 60' (and HT), OLS with match-clustered SE on score state, strength, home, prior xG diff and xG diff in the 15 min before the landmark (the trigger window), opponent early sub. Injury subs and red cards before the landmark excluded.
studies.data: StatsBomb open data, 23 full seasons/tournaments (2015/16 EPL, Serie A, Ligue 1; men's WC/Euro/Copa/AFCON; ISL; women's leagues and tournaments), 2,659 matches, 4,853 team-matches at the 60' landmark.
studies.split_check: xG-diff effect +0.028 in 2015/16 leagues, +0.048 elsewhere; same sign, neither CI excludes 0 alone.

studies.question: Should players hit a first serve on second serve?
studies.answer: No. 6 of 188 men and 4 of 112 women would gain. Median player loses 6.8 pts (men), 5.3 (women) per 100.
findings: Men: 152 of 188 lose with 95% CI below zero; 1 gain with CI above zero.
Women: 80 of 112 lose with 95% CI below zero; 0 gain with CI above zero.
Pooled men: 1st serve wins 44.6% per attempt vs 2nd 51.0%.
Pooled women: 1st serve wins 40.0% per attempt vs 2nd 45.4%.
studies.method: Per server: P(1st in) x P(win | 1st in) minus P(2nd in) x P(win | 2nd in). Bootstrap 95% CI resampling matches. Assumes first-serve in-rate and win rate hold on second-serve points.
studies.data: Match Charting Project points, 1960-2026 (71% of matches 2015+), 11,785 matches; servers with 500+ second serves.
studies.split_check: Gainers by era (250+ 2nd serves), pre-2015 / 2015+: men 4 of 104 / 14 of 193, women 3 of 42 / 7 of 169.

studies.question: Do players drop serve more often right after breaking?
studies.answer: No. Same player and match: hold rate after breaking is +0.7 pts (men), +0.5 (women) vs after opponent holds.
findings: Men: +0.7 pts (95% CI +0.2 to +1.2), 11,796 player-matches.
Women: +0.5 pts (95% CI -0.2 to +1.2), 7,616 player-matches.
Raw hold after breaking: men 82.0%, women 69.1%; mostly stronger servers breaking.
studies.method: Hold (non-tiebreak games) by whether the server broke in the previous game. Within player-match difference, weighted; bootstrap CI resampling matches. Form swings within a match bias this upward.
studies.data: Match Charting Project points, 11,270 matches, 249,107 service games.

studies.question: Do first serves wide, body and T win at equal rates, as mixed-strategy theory predicts?
studies.answer: Wide and T: yes, within 1 pt for the same server. Body: no, 4.2 pts lower (men), 4.1 (women).
findings: Within-player T minus wide: men -0.1 pts (SE 0.1, 498 player-sides), women -0.4 (SE 0.2, 311).
Wide vs T differ at p<.05 for 8% of men's and 7% of women's player-sides; 5% expected by chance.
Body minus wide/T, same server: men -4.2 pts (SE 0.2), women -4.1 (SE 0.2).
Body is 10% of men's and 20% of women's first serves; charters may log missed targets as body.
studies.method: Outcome: server wins the point, given the first serve was aimed at that target (faults count). Within-player test compares wide and T for each server and court side (150+ serves each).
studies.data: Match Charting Project points, 11,785 charted matches, 1,857,004 first serves with a direction.
studies.split_check: Wide vs T within 0.4 pts in both eras (pre-2015, 2015+), men and women.

studies.question: How much is the first pistol round worth, and does the side matter?
studies.answer: First pistol winner takes the map 59.5%: 57.1% on CT, 61.9% on T.
findings: Pistol 1 won on CT: map win 57.1% (56.1%-58.2%, n=8,809).
Pistol 1 won on T: map win 61.9% (60.9%-63.0%, n=8,716).
Both pistols: 69.3% map win (n=8,912). Split pistols, P1 winner: 49.4%.
Above Elo expectation: P1 on T +11.3 pp, on CT +6.0 pp. Win vs lose P1, Elo-adjusted: +17.2 pp (+16.0 to +18.6 pp).
studies.method: Map win % for pistol round winners (rounds 1 and 13), Wilson CIs. Team strength: logistic model with pre-map Elo; pistol effects as average marginal change, map-clustered CIs.
studies.data: bo3.gg round data, S/A/B-tier pro maps, 2023-10-16 to 2026-11-02, 17,525 maps
studies.split_check: P1 winner map win: early 59.3% (n=8,762), late 59.7% (n=8,763).

studies.question: After losing the pistol round, should the team save or buy on round 2?
studies.answer: Buying on round 2: +26.8 pp in round 2, -16.5 pp in round 3, map win -0.8 pp (not different from 0).
findings: CT buy vs save, adjusted: R2 +25.0 pp (+24.0 to +25.9 pp), R3 -17.0 pp (-18.6 to -15.5 pp). 66% of CT losers buy.
T buy vs save, adjusted: R2 +28.3 pp (+27.3 to +29.4 pp), R3 -16.0 pp (-17.6 to -14.5 pp). 50% of T losers buy.
Map win, buy vs save: CT -1.1 pp (-2.6 to +0.3 pp), T -0.8 pp (-2.2 to +0.7 pp).
First-half rounds won (of 12), buy vs save: CT +0.30 (+0.20 to +0.40), T +0.27 (+0.17 to +0.37).
studies.method: Pistol loser's round-2 buy class from bo3.gg equipment value (save = eco, buy = half/force). Logistic models adjust for side, team Elo, winner's round-2 equipment, loser's pistol kills and half; cluster-robust CIs by map.

studies.question: What does a stand-in cost an ESEA team?
studies.answer: About 2 pp beyond the five's own ratings, too small to beat held-out matches. Rate the five who play.
findings: After player Elo + FACEIT level of the five: first stand-in -0.09 log-odds (SE 0.04), second +0.16.
Held S58-S59 log loss: t -1.5, leave-one-day-out t -0.3. Not shipped.
Stand-in's FACEIT level counts like a core player's: .59 vs .54 log-odds per level (SE .08/.04).
studies.method: Core = 5 most-used players in the team's prior 20 maps that season (no lookahead). Logistic on the five's round-share player Elo and FACEIT level plus stand-in count, walk-forward ratings.
studies.data: FACEIT ESEA NA league, S53-S59, 18,217 matches; 6,078 with both cores defined

studies.question: How much does an equipment gap change round win chances on CT and T?
studies.answer: Full buy vs full buy: CT wins 51.7%. At equal dollar value CT wins 48.5%; an eco beats a full buy 5.6%.
findings: Full buy vs full buy: CT wins 51.7% (51.4%-52.0%, n=154,499).
Force vs full: CT forcing wins 36.0% (35.4%-36.5%, n=28,386); T forcing wins 36.0% (n=40,093).
Eco vs full: CT eco wins 5.9% (5.5%-6.4%, n=11,243); T eco wins 5.4% (n=17,966).
CT needs about $1.3k more equipment value than T for a 50% round (CT rifles and kits cost more).
studies.method: Non-pistol regulation rounds; equipment value at round start per team from bo3.gg, binned by CT minus T in $4k steps (ends capped at $24k). Round win rate with map-clustered CIs.
studies.data: bo3.gg round data, S/A/B-tier pro maps, 2023-10-16 to 2026-11-02, 17,525 maps, 327,073 rounds
studies.split_check: Full vs full CT win %: early 51.7% (n=76,815), late 51.7% (n=77,684).

studies.question: Does a losing streak hurt the next round beyond economy (the no-timeout baseline)?
studies.answer: No tilt. After 3+ straight losses a team wins +0.9 pp vs an economy and score model.
findings: After 1 loss in a row: wins 35.8%, model 36.3%, gap -0.4 pp (-0.7 to -0.2 pp, n=136,681).
After 3 losses in a row: wins 39.5%, model 38.5%, gap +1.1 pp (+0.7 to +1.5 pp, n=51,700).
After 5 losses in a row: wins 40.8%, model 40.0%, gap +0.8 pp (+0.1 to +1.6 pp, n=15,367).
bo3.gg round data has no timeout calls, so the timeout effect itself is not measured.
studies.method: Logistic baseline on buy-class matchup by side, equipment values, score gap, Elo and round in half; actual minus predicted win rate by current losing streak in the half, map-clustered CIs.
studies.data: bo3.gg round data, S/A/B-tier pro maps, 2023-10-16 to 2026-11-02, 17,525 maps, 327,073 rounds
studies.split_check: 3+ streak gap: early +0.9 pp (n=55,017), late +0.9 pp (n=55,026).

entries.short: Grade on the 20-80 scale of what a prospect becomes at peak: the mean outcome of past players with that profile.
body: 50 average regular, 60 plus, 70 star, 80 generational. Tiers every 5 points, grades in steps of 1.
Each board has its own outcome and rarity ladder. There is no shared cross-sport FV scale.
Headline = mean of the tier odds (busts and stars included), so it sits below the best case.
Graded on absolute talent from a fixed map fit on pooled history, not on rank within a class or board.
Strong classes get more high grades. Age and validated drivers adjust the grade.
entries.where: Every prospect board: CFB, CBB, hockey prospects, soccer prospects, tennis prospects; recruit tabs; MLB boards

entries.short: The realized outcome each FV tier stands for, set by rarity on each board.
body: CFB: NFL career (All-Pro, Pro Bowl, seasons as a starter), 2012-18 drafts.
CBB: peak NBA XPM, as rare as the matching NBA role (7+ All-NBA = 80), careers ending 2008-16.
Hockey: peak NHL WAR (best 3 of first 7 seasons), rarity in a draft class, 2008-19 classes.
Soccer: peak GAR at ages 22-26, rarity in a birth year and position group, players 22 in 2013-21.
Tennis: peak ranking points above No. 200 at ages 22-28, rarity in a birth year per tour, births 1979-97.
entries.where: fv model tab on each prospect page; FV conversion charts below

entries.short: Above each board's knot K the headline runs linear to 80 at T, so an 80 comes about once every 5 seasons.
body: Mean of a capped outcome cannot reach 80; the stretch makes 80 reachable but rare (Oct 31 2026).
K = mean that about 3 players a season reach; T = one player per about 5 seasons (exponential tail, held out).
Order is unchanged. The exact mean (fvx) stays in tooltips; above K the headline reads hotter than realized means.
entries.where: Headline FV on every prospect board (data/fv_scale.json)

entries.short: fvx = exact mean outcome; fvg = the pre-outcome grade the tier odds are computed from.
body: Headline FV = round(fvx), stretched above K. fvg feeds fits built on the grade (mock value, recruit stars).
The raw grade is not shown on the site; the outcome step stays (owner decision, Nov 1 2026).
entries.where: Data fields on CFB and CBB boards; tooltips

entries.short: Each player's odds of every outcome tier and their 10th-90th percentile outcome.
body: CFB and CBB: location-scale ordered probit of realized outcome on the grade; cut points at 30, 35 ... 70.
Spread terms kept only if held-out RPS improves (CFB: early season x2.1, walk-on, consensus, underclassman).
Held out: CFB RPS .0398 vs .0408 one spread; CBB .0767. Hockey, soccer, tennis: logistic odds per tier.
Shown in the player dropdown only; main boards show the single headline.

entries.term: Tier chances (NBA%, NHL%, Top%, Reg%, Star%)
entries.short: Chance of reaching a set outcome tier.
body: CBB NBA% = P(plays in the NBA), first rung of the FV model.
Hockey NHL% = 40+ (top 45 of a class); Reg% = 50+ (NHL regular, top 20 of a class).
Soccer Top% = 40+ (top-flight regular, top 250 of a birth year at position); Reg% = 50+ (top 90); Star% = 60+ (top 20).
entries.where: Board columns: CBB, hockey prospects, soccer prospects

entries.short: A + marks a player whose star odds beat the next 2.5 FV, from age.
body: Rule: + when P(60+ | FV, age) >= P(60+ | FV + 2.5). Only age passed held out as an upside signal.
Soccer held out t 5.0 / 4.1 at 55+ / 60+; tennis ATP t 4.3 / 3.3, WTA 3.9 / 3.1. Shares: tennis ~6%, soccer ~30% of top 2000.
CFB + rule failed held out (t -.71 / -.34) and was removed. CBB and hockey signals: none pass.
entries.where: Soccer prospects and tennis prospects boards

entries.short: A grade for a player off the source board: starts at the 20 floor and takes every available driver.
body: Ranked in FV order with a prov tag. CBB: ridge on height, weight, class, age, recruit rank, team top-8 FV (R2 .77).
Hockey: OHL, WHL, QMJHL, AHL and Liiga draft-eligibles off Tankathon, graded on NHLe, age, weight, position.
Soccer: academy-only and youth-international players get their own provisional line.
CFB: ESPN roster backups and carried-over players graded from the 20 floor.

entries.short: Held-out check of each board: graded FV band vs what the players became.
body: Per band: mean FV given vs reached (90% CI), predicted 40+/50+/60+ odds vs realized share.
Slopes: CFB .99, CBB .97, soccer 1.00, tennis ATP .99 / WTA .97; hockey calibrated.
Known heat: WTA 45-64 runs 2.5-4.8 hot; CFB 40+ odds 6-8 pts hot at FV 40-49.
entries.where: fv model tab, fv scorecard window

entries.short: An input enters an FV model only if it cuts held-out error.
body: Hockey, soccer, tennis: t >= 2 across held-out classes/seasons/birth years and wins two thirds of them.
CBB: dropping the driver must raise out-of-sample deviance in 4 of 5 folds (whole players held out).
CFB: multipliers refit leaving one draft class out; kept only if within-position r with NFL AV improves.
entries.where: fv model tabs (drivers kept, out-of-sample evidence)

entries.short: NFL outcome grade for every FBS and FCS player.
body: Composite: production (Stat+, Marcel 5/4/3, regressed), On3 talent, age, frame, combine, badges, XV parts.
Composite rank per class maps to FV by measured NFL outcome counts per position (drafts 2012-18).
Scouting consensus (9 boards + Kiper top 25) blended at weight .5 at full coverage.
Then the outcome step (ordered probit), mean headline, stretched top. Positional value scales elite RB, LB, DL, TE, S.
entries.where: CFB board, draft board, fv model tab

entries.short: NBA outcome grade for every D-I player and listed internationals.
body: E[FV] = 20 + 10 P(30+) + 10 P(40+) + 10 P(50+) + (mean 60+ career - 50) P(60+); one ridge logistic per rung.
Newcomers: recruit rank (On3, 247, Barttorvik), class. Returners: 3-season BPM, conference power, age, size, rates.
Board stage adds June draft-board rank and guard combine testing. E maps to a grade on pooled 2009-16 boards.
In season: E = (1 - w) preseason + w now, w = minutes / (minutes + k); k 63 newcomers, 128 returners.
entries.where: CBB board, fv model tab, in season window

entries.short: OLS on outcome FV for the draft class and drafted players short of 100 NHL games.
body: Draft model kept: log slot (board rank as slot), draft-year NHLe, defense, goalie, CHL first-round pick, class strength.
Leave-one-class-out error 89.86 vs 95.14 for slot alone (2008-19 classes, 2,541 picks).
After the draft: stage models add latest NHLe, pro games, World Juniors spot, NHL games and WAR so far.
entries.where: Hockey prospects board, drafted prospects, fv model tab

entries.short: OLS on outcome FV for every under-22 in 33 leagues plus academy and feeder leagues.
body: Inputs kept include age, market value (deflated to the fit seasons' level), GAR this and last season,
minutes share, club strength, scoring rate, height, position, PL2 minutes. 53,680 rows, 2013-20.
Held out by birth cohort: error 55.65 vs 64.42 for age and market value alone (R2 .42).
entries.where: Soccer prospects board, fv model tab

entries.short: Hurdle model for every ATP and WTA player under 22 with a ranking or a pro match in the last year.
body: Logistic for any peak value, OLS on outcome FV given value: FV = (1 - p) x 20 + p x mean given value.
ATP kept: age, rank, unranked, Elo, 52-week win rate, years since pro debut, Futures volume.
WTA kept: age, rank, unranked, Elo, rank x age, tour-qualifying volume. Held out by birth year; OOS R2 .50 / .46.
Height is never an input (the archive fills height for players who made it: a leak).
entries.where: Tennis prospects ATP and WTA boards, fv model tab

entries.short: Projected RWA over the next year against tier-1 starters, 20-80 (50 = average tier-1 starter).
body: Prospect = under 20 maps at S-tier events. Projection: rating, age, share of last year's rounds at S/A-tier events.
S/A share is negative on top of the rating's tier lift (held t -4.9). Rise and every stat line failed.
Quarterly cutoffs, fit 2024-25, held out from Jul 2025; a term ships only past the Bonferroni cut of its batch.
Badges (top 25% on a stat) tested on prospects and the main board: none passed, so CS2 shows none.

entries.short: Baseball boards are graded by hand on the FanGraphs 20-80 tiers.
body: No model. Tiers: 80 top 5 overall (7+ WAR a season), 60 All-Star (3.4-4.9), 50 average regular (1.6-2.4).
Boards: 2026 draft hitters v1 (May 7), U19 MiLB prospects, White Sox org top 64.
entries.where: Baseball page (draft hitters, U19 MiLB, White Sox org, fv scale)

entries.short: Projected FV for high school recruits.
body: CFB xFV = P(on board) x FV if on + (1 - P(on)) x 20, year 1; hurdle fit on ESPN 2023-26 classes.
CFB recruit profile weighed on NFL outcomes of 2011-19 classes; the board sets the level.
CBB: hurdle on consensus rank and old-for-class; P(reach NBA) then log(FV - 20) given NBA; trained 2009-16.
entries.where: Recruits tabs: 2027-2029 classes, class rankings, recruit model

entries.short: Recruit star rating cut from the projected FV, not the industry stars.
body: CFB: 5-star+ top 6 a class, 5 top 3% of board FV, 4 top 10%, 3 above median, 2 on board, 1 off board (year-3 xFV).
CBB: 5 = 2+ NBA seasons as a starter, 4 = reached the NBA, 3 = D-I starter at BPM +3, 2 = played D-I, 1 = did not.
Arrow = ARK stars minus industry stars.

entries.short: Bronze to platinum trait medals by the name: one stat each, regressed by volume.
body: Tiers at the 75/90/97/99th percentile of the position. CFB badges build archetypes.
On other boards a badge shows only if it predicts the sport's own outcome held out beyond the value metric.
Display only: no badge feeds FV or projections. Volume and usage traits pass; efficiency rates mostly fail.
entries.where: Every board (medals by the name), player cards

entries.short: Each player's grade at their best season, listed by position.
body: CFB rebuilds every FBS season 2014-25; box-score era (2014-18) means recalibrated to NFL outcomes.
Other boards read their past lists; only grade-complete rows are used.
entries.where: all-time FV tab on CFB, CBB, hockey, soccer and tennis prospect pages

entries.short: Wins over a replacement starter in a 12-game season.
body: WAR = snap share x (line + weight x quality) x .227; 1 pt of margin a game = .0189 win% (928 FBS team seasons).
Line = margin lost when an average starter sits: QB 2.7, RB 1.7, EDGE 1.4, WR 1.35, CB 1.3, S 1.1, DT 1.0, LB 1.0.
Quality from Stat+, badges and FV. QB keeps 1.25 pts per SD; the rest goes to offensive teammates by snaps.
Replacement lineup wins .18 (2 of 12); an average team's starters total 3.8 WAR.
entries.where: CFB board, WAR leaders tab, team talent

entries.short: WAR minus snap share x line: wins over an average starter at the position.
body: Comparable across positions; below average < 0.

entries.short: WAR with quality from the stat-line parts that track winning.
body: CFB: PFN score plus position parts (QB cmp %, yds/att, INT rate; OL pressure rate; DT splash; CB yds/target).
Fit on 2024-25 team margin. Held out team r .88 vs .86 for WAR quality; win% r .73 vs .68.
NFL: same idea fit to team margin per game; on missed games t 4.9 vs 2.1 for AV WAR.
Next-season forecasts tie with WAR, so projections and game models stay on WAR.
entries.where: CFB and NFL WAR leaders tabs (XV column)

entries.short: Wins over replacement: .6 x AV WAR + .4 x XV, season to date.
body: AV WAR = (AV - replacement AV at the sub-position x snap share) x .091 wins per AV.
.091 from team wins on team AV (160 team seasons 2021-25, r .86). Replacement team wins 3 of 17.
Defensive AV rebuilt from pressures, stops and plays on the ball. Two-way players earn WAR on each side.
entries.where: NFL WAR leaders, team WAR, rookies, breakouts

entries.short: Production index: 100 + 25 x z of the position all-in-one score this season.
body: Source score: PFN QB+, RB+, WR+, TE+, OLi, EDGE+, DT+, LB+, CB+, SAF+; K and P by percentile.
z against the snap-weighted position mean, FBS or FCS. 125 = 1 SD above average.
FV production driver; validity vs NFL AV: TE .52, WR .50, QB .48, RB .48, EDGE .40, LB .40, DT .37.
entries.where: CFB board, WAR leaders, true freshmen

entries.short: xNIL = NIL market worth now; yNIL = estimated pay entering the season; zNIL = xNIL - yNIL.
body: xNIL = position price x on-field value (AV at FV, x playing time), shared within P4 and G5 pools.
yNIL = program budget split by a preseason index (P4 ~$20M, G5 ~$3M, FCS ~$0.4M a program).
Not fit to On3 valuations (they move only +18% per 10 FV). zNIL growth is 20% of each coach score.
FCS players at FBS-starter FV priced at 40% of the FBS rate. CBB xNIL: minutes share x (BPM + 3) at school price.
entries.where: CFB board, team talent, team builder, fv to xNIL charts; CBB recruits

entries.short: College on-field value a season: snap share x position weight x quality.
body: Quality = Stat+ z + .5 badge z + .25 FV z. Team R2 vs 2026 SRS .63 vs .44 for summed FV value.
Used for college injury cost and team value; NFL value stays on AV at FV.
entries.where: CFB team talent (Season AV), fv to war chart

entries.short: NBA impact: .5 databallr DPM + .5 Basketball-Reference BPM, points per 100 possessions over average.
body: Shown shrunk by minutes: raw x MP / (MP + 300) + role mean x 300 / (MP + 300).
Role mean = -1 + .5 ln(1 + MP82 / 100). Fit on next-season XPM 2011-26 (RMSE 1.26 vs 1.59 raw).
Raw XPM feeds game models, VORX and the CBB board target. BPM only where no DPM row (*).
entries.where: NBA XPM leaders, rookies, contract value, depth chart

entries.short: NBA wins over replacement: .030 x (XPM + 1.4) x MP / 48.
body: Replacement XPM -1.4; both constants fit to team wins (480 team seasons 2011-26). Default sort of the XPM board.
entries.where: NBA XPM leaders, projections, contract value

entries.short: Season-to-date XPM blended with a preseason prior by minutes.
body: prior + (XPM - prior) x MP / (k + MP); k 509 veterans, 809 newcomers (7,269 player seasons 2012-26).
80% range covers .806 / .799 held out. Display only.

entries.short: Projected VORX x market $ per win, minus salary, every year left.
body: $ per win = payroll above the minimum / league projected VORX = $12.65M (2026-27); +7% a year (assumption).
Player option counted only when it pays the player; team option only when it pays the team.

entries.short: Projected Barttorvik BPM this season.
body: Ridge on last season, recruiting, age, size; in season blends to-date BPM.
Team context (Nov 3 2026): returning teammates' WAR, teammates' recruiting (top 8 -ln rank), WAA, transfer up/down.
Forward 2020-26 RMSE: returners 2.558 -> 2.462 (t 18), newcomers 3.439 -> 3.229 (t 14). Not an FV input.

entries.short: Wins over a replacement / average D-I player.
body: WAR = (BPM + 2) x minutes / 40 x team possessions a 40 / 100 x .0124 wins a point; WAA uses BPM.
Replacement BPM -2.0 = the 9th man in team minutes (2025-26). Wins a point fit on 365 team seasons:
wins = .41 x games + team WAR (r .85). The textbook slope (.0347 at margin sd 11.5) overstates: schedules
pair strong with strong and win odds flatten at the ends. FV test: WAR, WAA, career and 5/4/3 WAR fail.
entries.where: CBB WAR leaders, stats, portal, returning

entries.short: BPM against the position: 100 + 25 x z.
body: z = (BPM - position mean) / position sd; G .10 / 3.85, F .50 / 4.05, C .52 / 4.31 (10%+ minute seasons 2008-16).
FV driver (Nov 3 2026): passes three fold rules (t 2.9-3.5, 4-5/5), held 2017-19 (+.17) and forward 2020-23 (+.26).
entries.where: CBB stats, WAR leaders, portal; FV inputs

entries.short: Hollinger single-game value.
body: PTS + .4 FGM - .7 FGA - .4 (FTA - FTM) + .7 ORB + .3 DRB + STL + .7 AST + .7 BLK - .4 PF - TOV.
FV and xBPM tests (a game, a 40, best game, 20+ games): all fail.

entries.short: 1st-2nd year players above their preseason projection.
body: xBPM up = live xBPM - preseason xBPM (minutes-blended). Also BPM over x, minutes, usage and FV gains.
Last season view: 2nd-years against their freshman line (WAR, BPM, minutes, usage gains).
FV tests: WAR gain, minutes gain, usage gain, BPM x (1 - minutes share) all fail (low-minute BPM passes the folds, not the top of the board).

entries.short: Team tables: last season's minutes and WAR back; roster grades.
body: Ret Min% = last season's minutes still on the roster (Barttorvik ids). In WAR = incoming transfers' WAR.
Talent = mean FV of the top 8. xNBA = sum of NBA%. TvE = talent rank - ARK rank.
FV tests: vacated minutes (opportunity), returning teammates' WAR, teammates' recruiting fail; the last two pass for xBPM.

entries.short: CBB FV target: mean of a career's best three NBA XPM seasons, each shrunk toward -2 by 500 minutes.
body: FV bands start at the XPM as many careers reached as reached the matching NBA role. See the CBB chart.

entries.short: Descriptive wins over replacement at goal value.
body: 5v5 on-ice xG vs teammates, PP xG /5, PK /4, finishing (goals - ixG), penalties, share of team leftover xG.
Goalies: GSAx at full credit. Sums to team goal differential (R2 .975).
Replacement = players outside each team's top 13 F / 7 D / 2 G.
entries.where: NHL WAR leaders, rookies; hockey prospect outcome

entries.short: Projected WAR and projected goals per 60 over an average player.
body: HPM = Marcel-weighted (1 / .7 / .5) shrunk rates, components weighted by how well they carry to next season.
pWAR = (HPM - replacement) x TOI / 60 / goals per win. LOSO R2 .38 vs .23 before (t 4.95, 15/17 seasons).
Goalie GSAx barely repeats (weight .07), so goalie pWAR ~0.4 while goalie WAR runs ~7.
entries.where: NHL WAR leaders, backup watch, rookies

entries.short: Goals saved above expected (MoneyPuck xG).
body: Goalie tab shows GSAx a game shrunk toward a new goalie's level; feeds the NHL totals model.

entries.short: NHL points a full season at a league's translation factor.
body: Factors fit on every pick's career since 2008 from league pairs, a year of age development removed.
Shrunk toward the published factor by link count. CHL leagues ~.10-.12, NCAA ~.21.

entries.short: Goals above replacement on one scale across leagues.
body: Shrunk per-90 rates (on-ice, npxG, xA, xGBuildup, keeper saves) weighted to next-season team goal difference.
Replacement per position from players under 900 minutes. League strength counts. Held out R2 .61.
PAR = GAR x points per goal of difference (.626).
entries.where: Soccer player value, rookies, backup watch

entries.short: Team-share value: minutes / 90 x (club rating - replacement) / 11.
body: Club rating = goals a match vs an average big-five club; replacement -2.5 (a bottom Scotland/Greece/Denmark side).
Outcome = mean of the best three GAR seasons at ages 22-26. Differs from the senior GAR above.

entries.short: Estimated market value in EUR millions with no market input.
body: Ridge on log Transfermarkt value: GAR now and past two seasons, minutes, age, position, league, club.
Held out R2 .68 (Oct) to .78 (Jul). Gap to TM forecasts TM's next move (slope .23, 12/12 seasons).

entries.short: Elo on every pro match since 1991 at every level; Elo+ against players the same age.
body: K = 250 / (matches + 5)^0.4, Slams x1.1, start 1500. Elo+ = 100 + 25 per SD vs same-age players with 20+ matches.
entries.where: Tennis prospects board, tennis ARK Ranking

entries.short: Round win % a Counter-Strike player adds per round, opponent-adjusted; 0 = average tier-1 starter.
body: Box: team round share on its five per-round stat lines (kills, deaths, assists, ADR, KAST, openings, trades,
multi-kills, clutches, headshots, damage taken). Plus-minus: half the round share the box misses, split across the five.
No utility measure: bo3.gg has no flash or utility damage data; utility $ bought failed (t -2.5), accuracy hurt.
Tier lift: +0.5 x share of last year's rounds at S/A-tier events (low-tier pools link to the top through few maps).
Opponents credited x1.0, half-life 180 days, 25 rounds of shrink. Held out R2 .131 vs .120 Nov 2, .108 K-D.

entries.short: Serve and return points won over the average top-100 player, opponent-adjusted.
body: Percentage points, hard court. xHold / xBreak = games held or broken vs an average top-100 opponent via the game chain.

entries.short: Points a game over a replacement QB from the game model's QB term.
body: Rating = weighted career EPA/play shrunk toward replacement (-0.12) with 250 pseudo-plays.

entries.short: Kick and punt return yards over expected, shrunk.
body: YOE = return yards minus the mean return from the same spot (5-yard bins, this season). Yards, not EPA (EPA does not repeat).
entries.where: special teams tab on NFL and CFB pages

entries.short: Outcome per recruit over what their recruiting rating predicted, shrunk by sample.
body: CFB: NFL FV per signee, school tau .42 FV, rolling t 5.3 (6/6). CBB NBA FV is null; college BPM delta passes.
CBB head coach BPM over expected: split t 5.1. Shown with +/- 1 SD.
entries.where: development tab on CFB and CBB pages

entries.short: P(declares) x P(picked in the 2027 draft).
body: Declare: logit on ln xPick and age on draft day; ranked underclassmen ~94%, seniors ~69%, RS seniors 100%.
Picked: log-normal around the mock xPick; the SD narrows toward the draft (PFF dated boards, 2020-26).

entries.short: P(on another FBS or FCS roster next season).
body: Ridge logit on the 2024-25 and 2025-26 cycles: class, production, role, recruit rank, record, P(HC change), distance from home.
Out-of-time AUC .738. Transfer% + stay + exit = 100%. NIL-era data only (July 2021 on).

entries.short: P(on an FBS roster next season) for FCS players.
body: Logit on 2023-26 FCS-to-FBS moves: production, team strength, year in school, position. Capped at 1 - Draft%.

entries.short: P(on a D-I roster next season) for D-II and D-III players.
body: Ridge logit on NCAA D-II/III box scores, 2023-24 and 2024-25 move-ups: production, starts, minutes, team SRS, division.
Out of time on 2025-26 to 2026-27: AUC .899, log loss .077 vs .111 base rate.
FV = 20 + D-1% x V. V: his line translated to a first D-I season (shrunk BPM; ridge on 318 movers, out of time r .43/.60),
then what 2009-16 arrivals with that season and class became (Poisson index + monotone map, out-of-fold deviance t 2.8).

entries.short: Chance a college player leaves school for this NBA draft.
body: Recruit rank, minutes-shrunk BPM, class, era; plus the midseason board rank. Seniors and internationals 100%.

entries.short: 20th, 50th and 80th percentile of WAR, VORX and stats, full season and rest of season.
body: Rest of season = rate x exposure (minutes, TOI, snaps); rate = Marcel 1 / .7 / .5 with fitted shrink.
Recalibrated per season-left bin; checked by PIT on held-out seasons (+/- .03 overall).
entries.where: projections tab on NFL, NBA, NHL pages

entries.short: Per-game points, rebounds, assists (NBA, CBB) and fantasy lines (NFL, CFB).
body: NBA walks the game model's minutes and P(play), plus pace, opponent, minutes freed by teammates out.
Held out 2024-26 PRA MAE 6.20 vs 6.46 for season average; CBB 5.42 vs 5.58.

entries.short: Projection minus the replacement projection at the position, 12-team league.
body: Replacement = first non-starter: QB13, RB30, WR31, TE13, K13, DST13. Overall rank by VOR.

entries.short: Young players' weekly WAR over expected.
body: xWAR = WAR rate a snap before the week (three seasons shrunk to the group, updated in season) x snaps.

entries.short: 1st-2nd year QB/RB/WR/TE whose touches and targets are rising.
body: Lists usage growth; it is a watch list, not a model grade.

entries.short: Second and third-string players graded above a starter.
body: Gap = backup value - starter value (FV in college; WAR, XPM, HPM or GAR in the pros). College listed at gap >= 3.
Rank by xGap = the gap projected over two seasons, adding the age (or class) gap; held out t -3.0 to -15.6.
entries.where: backup watch tab on every sport page

entries.short: Nearest historical profiles shown in the player dropdown.
body: CFB: nearest 2014-22 profiles. Hockey stage 3-4 comps also feed FV (held-out pass); elsewhere display only.

entries.short: Each sport's power ranking: the game model's neutral-site rating, ranked.
body: Same number the game model uses, so picks already read it. Split into parts (Elo, efficiency, talent ...).
Rank range = 80% range of true rank from 4,000 draws at the rating sd measured on past seasons.
CBB 2016-26: ARK picks the winner 77.3% vs AP 76.8%, Coaches 77.1% vs 76.7%.
entries.where: ARK Ranking tab on every sport page; ARKRANKING page

entries.short: Points vs an average FBS team, neutral field.
body: Elo (preseason prior: last season, SP+, 247 talent, returning production, transfers) + opponent-adjusted EPA/play.
Plus home, rest, travel, altitude, FCS, special teams, P4 tier, 4th-down aggressiveness, returning production,
game control. Sim win sd 14.2. Current injuries charged (Inj); Full = at full strength.
entries.where: CFB ARK Ranking, games, season odds

entries.short: Expected margin vs an average team, neutral field, with this week's QB and injuries.
body: Fitted terms: Elo, starting QB, rest, home, injuries, market rating from earlier closes, return game.
Injury cost = WAR a game x 36 pts a win x P(miss); questionable .25, doubtful .98.
entries.where: NFL ARK Ranking, games, season odds

entries.short: Expected margin vs an average D-I team on a neutral floor.
body: Fitted terms: adjusted efficiency x possessions, Elo, home, game control, conference home game, injuries,
home x attendance, ESPN BPI, form, preseason injury report. Preseason prior from returning minutes, transfers, top-5 FV.
Luck-stripped: 50% of three-point luck removed.
entries.where: CBB ARK Ranking, games, season odds, tournament odds

entries.short: Expected margin vs an average team, neutral floor, current roster and today's injury report.
body: Fitted terms: Elo, net rating, market rating, home, lineup value (XPM x minutes x chance to play), playoff Elo, rest.
25% of three-point luck removed. Proj column (rest-of-season VORX) is display only.
entries.where: NBA ARK Ranking, games, season odds

entries.short: Win chance from a logistic on Elo, expected-goals rating, back-to-back, home and lineup value.
body: xG rating: opponent-adjusted ridge, half-life 120 days, .7 carried over a season. Lineup value follows trades.
Totals use xG, goals, market total and the starting goalie.
entries.where: NHL ARK Ranking, games, season odds

entries.short: Goals a match vs an average big-five club, neutral ground; one scale for every league.
body: Online Poisson attack and defence within each league; league strength from cross-league matches only.
Inputs blended walk-forward: market-implied goals from earlier closes, xG (Understat, FotMob), squad value.
Dixon-Coles rho -.04. Big five vs close, held out: log loss .972 vs .967.
entries.where: Soccer ARK Ranking, league tabs, UEFA cups, MLS

entries.short: Win chance vs the average top-50 player, best of three, over the tour's 52-week surface mix.
body: Surface Elo blended with a games-won rating and opponent-adjusted serve and return point ratings (Markov chain).
Fit on 2012-22 tour main draws; held 2023-26 log loss ~.596 vs Elo .603.

entries.short: Series win chance vs the average top-20 team.
body: Player Elo that follows players between rosters (per map, on round share), bo3.gg team map rating with veto,
region offsets, Valve VRS points and the five players' mean RWA. Held out log loss .553 vs VRS .667. No picks: no free closing odds history.

entries.short: Map win chance vs the average top-20 team on each map in the pool.
body: bo3.gg team map rating: team Elo plus a team x map offset, both moved per map on round share; offsets start at 0, so thin maps stay near the team's level.
Shown on the map-win scale (round-share logit x 2.43, fit on 124k maps). Match cards show the projected veto: each side bans its worst and picks its best, higher-ranked side first.
Display only: the series model already uses the veto as a term.

entries.short: Chance to reach each stage and win the next Major, from simulated events.
body: 20,000 simulations of Valve's Major format from the series model: three 16-team Swiss stages (Bo1, Bo3 for elimination and advancement; Stage 3 all Bo3), then an 8-team single-elimination playoff.

Pairing per the Major rulebook: round 1 seed i v i+8, highest v lowest seed without a rematch, priority table in rounds 4-5, seeds by record, Buchholz, initial seed. Invites from Valve's invitation standings; drawn pairings and results replace simulated ones.
Each simulation draws every team's strength once (sd 0.45 logit, picked on stages before Jul 2025), so rating error carries through the event.

Backtest, S-tier events held out from Jul 2025: Swiss advancement log loss 9.63 per stage vs 9.92 on VRS points alone (11 of 15 stages, t -0.75); bracket titles 1.63 vs 1.72 (15 of 26, t -0.94). Better on both, not significant at this sample.
entries.where: Counter-Strike event odds, ARKRANKING title odds

entries.short: Results-and-margin rating; 1500 = average.
body: CFB Elo starts from a preseason prior. CS2 Elo: +400 = 10 to 1 odds. Tennis Elo on wins, every level.

entries.short: How much of each game a team spent with the win in hand.
body: Time-weighted win chance from score and clock only, opponent-adjusted, carried across seasons.
Shipped in CFB (held out MAE t -4.1) and CBB (t -2.0). NBA failed.

entries.short: Talent = projected starters' value by FV; TvE = Elo vs the Elo talent predicts, in SD.
body: CFB Talent = sum over the projected starting 22 of expected college WAR a season at FV. TvE > 0 = above talent.

entries.short: 10,000 simulated seasons from the game model.
body: Rating error sd shrinks with the season left (sd^2 = a + b x share left, measured on past seasons).
xW = wins so far + simulated rest. Outputs: conference, playoff, title odds; full NFL tiebreakers.

entries.short: Committee model plus bracket for the 12-team playoff.

2026 rules: P4 champions in, best G6 champion, Notre Dame if top 12; top 4 byes.

entries.short: Committee and bracket sims for bids, seeds and rounds.

Conference tournaments and the bracket played with the game model.

entries.short: Our title, conference and division sims vs DraftKings futures (vig removed).
body: Display only; win-total backtests found no proven edge (NBA b .22 t 3.0 in sample, held out t 1.5).

entries.short: Team trait medals, one stat each, shrunk by games to reliability .5.

entries.short: Head coach and coordinator scores; coach market value vs public pay.
body: Pay is program plus wins (USA Today data); Surplus = Value - Pay. Staff score includes zNIL growth (20%).
Coach value-added does not carry to a new job (failed test); staff weights are set by hand.
entries.where: CFB staff, coach pay, coaching jobs tabs

entries.short: Model line, win chance and projected score for every game.
body: Margin from the sport's rating (see Team ratings); win chance = normal (or logistic) on the margin.
Win sd fit walk-forward: NBA ~12, CBB 11.9, CFB 14.2. Totals: separate model per sport.
Predictions is the only page with picks, lines and props; sport pages show projections only.
entries.where: games and game table tabs; Predictions

entries.short: Each game is predicted with a model fit only on games before it.
body: Seasons split into tuning (terms enter) and held out (report and veto). Errors clustered by game day.
Game models tab compares live loss to the walk-forward expectation for the same month.

entries.short: Shared rule for every model term.
body: Evidence = Stouffer z of tuning and held-out t (drop-one). One Benjamini-Hochberg family over all terms.
Keep at q <= .10; drop at q > .10 when held-out loss is no worse without it; otherwise watch.
Terms past 365 days are flagged for re-test.

entries.short: Model minus the market, in points (spread, total) or chance (moneyline, tennis).
body: Edge % on the full table = raw model chance minus the no-vig market chance.
Gaps past 5 sd are treated as bad lines; picks between 3 and 5 sd are staked at the cap.

entries.short: A pick is the model's side when |model - line| >= X for that sport and market.
body: X = smallest gap whose calibrated return at -103 is > 0 on tuning seasons.
A market or segment is on only if held-out picks beat the close (clvRet > 0, t >= 1.65, n >= 30).
One pick a game per market family. Bet to = worst line that still clears X.

entries.short: Expected return at the price, from held-out picks judged by the close.
body: Edge = min(EV, a + b (gap - mean gap)); a blends close value and ROI; b = the market's own slope, shrunk.
History priced at Novig -103. TIMING .5 halves every backtest edge (live bets come after part of the move).
NBA backtest edge also x.5 (history saw tip-time injury news the open did not).

entries.short: Stake as % of bankroll: full Kelly on the calibrated edge, compounding.
body: Formerly Dengler Units (DU); 1 DU = 1% of bankroll. Picks qualify where the edge at the price > 0.
Cap 5% a bet (tennis 2%). Joint slate Kelly gave the same growth as per-pick (rho ~0).
Walk-forward: 1x Kelly most log growth at the backtest edge and at half of it.
entries.where: Predictions picks, game table, paper book

entries.short: Open picks on one ET date, all sports, scaled to at most 40% of bankroll.
body: Stake x min(1, 40 / total). Walk-forward: P(50% drawdown) .12 vs .27 uncapped at 1x edge.

entries.short: Every pick is judged first by the closing line, ROI second.
body: Close = last snapshot before the start. CLV = points the line moved our way.
Worth at close (clvRet) = return the pick was worth at the closing price, with t.
CLV needs far fewer bets than results for t 2 (CBB 5+ pts: ~228 vs ~402).
entries.where: Predictions picks, paper book, picks backtest

entries.short: Opening lines that mirror the close or move more than 6 sd (median-based) are dropped from history.
body: Mirrored opens were home/away swaps (mostly 2025-26 CBB neutral sites) that inflated backtests.

entries.short: Predicts the close from the open and the model gap (market softness b).
body: close - open = b x (model - open) + controls. b: CFB spread .10, CFB total .22, CBB .10, NBA spread .24, total .42.
Break-even gap = where a -110 bet at the open breaks even at the predicted close.

entries.short: Model total minus the mean model-line gap over the slate and the season's last 100 games.
body: Keeps totals picks from being a bet on league scoring level. CFB, NBA and (since Nov 1) CBB.

entries.short: The posted picks graded at posted line, price and Kelly %, compounding.
body: Identical to the picks tab since Oct 28 2026; reset Oct 28 15:35Z. No real money.

entries.short: Live switch that stops a losing pick rule until a refit.
body: Judged after 50+ picks: stop if last 300 clustered t < -1 or CUSUM S = max(0, S - clvRet / sd - .25) >= 10.
entries.where: Predictions picks backtest (rule monitor), game models tab

entries.short: Sequential test of each rule's live close value vs its backtest.
body: H1 = backtest edge x TIMING; H0 = 0. Pause at 19:1 for no edge; confirm at 19:1 for the edge.
About 120 (NBA/CBB totals) to 275 (CFB totals) bets to a verdict.

entries.short: Held-out log growth a season at the close, and chance of a 25% / 50% fall from peak.
body: Resampled from walk-forward picks. Full Kelly accepts high drawdown risk over long seasons.

entries.short: One prop per player per game, full Kelly at Novig prices, week scaled to a budget.
body: P(over) from projection shape by decile, shrunk .414. Held out 2025-26: 3,732 bets 55.3%, t 3.1 at -110.
Weekly budget 50% of bankroll until ~300 props are graded.

entries.short: Model side when it differs from the Novig no-vig price by 4+ points of win chance.
body: Calibrated chance = no-vig + .5 x k toward the model (k .25 logits). Cap 2% a bet.
Tour-level main draws; tuned 2025, held out 2026: 1,935 picks, +4.5% worth at close (t 19).

entries.short: Every game whose model winner is -200 to +200, or the market underdog (flip).
body: Display only, not a pick rule. Held-out flip record: all +1.2% t .6.

entries.short: Markets tested and off because they did not beat the close.
body: NHL (ML and totals), soccer (1X2, O/U 2.5, MLS, props), CS2 (no free closing odds), NBA/NHL props.
Their game projections still show; Kelly % reads off.

entries.short: Predictive, blended and conviction mock drafts for the NFL, NBA and NHL drafts.
body: Predictive = projection of the real draft: consensus boards plus model (CFB board weight .75-.85 backtested).
Conviction = the model board (FV before the consensus blend) plus team fit.
Blended = each slot at the geometric mean of the two xPicks. Predictive and conviction grade each other.
entries.where: mock draft group on CFB, CBB, hockey prospects pages

entries.short: Expected pick: geometric blend of consensus average rank and rank by our draft value.
body: Market weight .55 + .3 x sqrt(boards / 9); unranked prospects .65 at 1.3x the boards' depth.
Past the last pick = projected undrafted (UDFA signings tab).

entries.short: Teams pick on -ln(xPick) + need weight x need.
body: Need from the whole NFL position room: rookie-deal draft capital or salary, cut for age and expiring deals.
Penalties for doubling up, a set QB and position runs. QB top-pick premium decays by pick.

entries.short: Projected trades on Massey-Thaler pick values; real traded picks from Wikipedia.
body: Trades in every round (5, 7, 6, 5, 5, 2, 1 a round); next-year picks at .48 of a mid-round pick.
Solid tag = traded pick; dashed tag = projected trade.

entries.short: A pick the other mock takes 2.5x+ and 16+ picks later (reach) or earlier (value).
body: Site table only; the GFX drops the chips.

entries.short: Simulated drafts give each prospect's pick range.

entries.short: Consensus of 2027 boards (.5 median rank + .5 mean) and conviction on slot plus college line.

Entrants: Dec% draws; FV 40+ rule for the pool.

entries.short: The draft slot a board rank points to.

Consensus boards: PFN industry (7 analysts), Tankathon, PFF, Kiper. Conference availability reports.

NBA and NHL 2x daily; soccer 2x daily; tennis 2x daily; CS2 every 4 h; soccer and tennis prospects daily.
